tier_reason: Issue #35 (paul-fornage, 2026-06-01) is an informal in-app observation: 'x86 is like twice as fast as image' and the image crate is faster on a Raspberry Pi 5 at higher qualities, with no harness, no x86 CPU model, no flags and no measured figures; the repo's own criterion/ benches (encode, fdct, ycbcr) only time jpeg-encoder itself. Approximate words without a measurement are directional, so D.

corrections.stars_or_usage: 33 stars, 13 forks; crates.io 8,025,519 total downloads (1,404,009 recent) and 83 reverse dependencies, including zune-image, pdf-writer, kornia-io, dicom-transfer-syntax-registry, tiff-writer and makepad-studio
corrections.caveats: No benchmark against libjpeg-turbo, mozjpeg or the image crate is published. The criterion/ bench crate (benches encode, fdct, ycbcr) depends only on jpeg-encoder with its internal 'benchmark' feature and compares its own scalar and SIMD paths. The only outside comparison is issue #35, an informal observation inside the reporter's app (not a cargo bench): roughly 2x faster than the image crate on x86 (no CPU model, flags or numbers), slower than the image crate at higher qualities on a Raspberry Pi 5 (Cortex-A76), and the std_simd branch about 5% slower than main. The 'simd' feature is AVX2-only per the README, which explains the ARM gap. justin13888/image-evaluation includes it as a tested encoder, but its repo README carries no results (canonical run is on a website not reachable here). Low star count, but widely used as a dependency (8.0M crates.io downloads, 83 reverse dependencies).

tier_reason: No benchmark page exists. The README 'How fast is it?' section only points to examples/PNGenc_Test, which times one 128x128 generated image with micros() (writing to an SD card by default) and compares nothing. linux/main.cpp has no timing code, and function_test.ino only checks output sizes.

corrections.license: Apache-2.0 (src/ also vendors zlib 1.2.11 deflate.c, trees.c, crc32.c, adler32.c and zutil.c under the zlib license)
corrections.stars_or_usage: 49 stars, 12 forks, 31 commits; NLnet NGI Zero Core funded (ImageCodes-Optimised project)
corrections.caveats: No speed claim against libpng, lodepng, stb_image_write or any other encoder in the README or examples. examples/PNGenc_Test/PNGenc_Test.ino times one 128x128 8-bpp indexed image with micros() and, by default (WRITE_TO_SD), includes SD-card writes. examples/function_test/function_test.ino declares timing variables but only checks output sizes and the PNG magic bytes. linux/main.cpp prints no timings (Makefile: -O2). Compression is a vendored copy of zlib 1.2.11 deflate, the same deflate libpng normally uses, so it has no reason to be faster than libpng on desktop CPUs. It targets low RAM (runs on MCUs with at least 45K free RAM, no malloc) rather than speed. Tier D, low notability (49 stars); kept because the seed list asked for it.

notes: Record accurate apart from the license (vendored zlib files) and a small caveat error: function_test.ino does not print timings. The vendored zlib 1.2.11 deflate means no throughput edge over libpng is expected. Last commit 2025-11-17 is confirmed, so it is still active.
